The release that turns a working internal tool into a plugin: dry runs everywhere, access by
capability, and the first test suite. 103 tests across PHP 8.1–8.4 and Moodle 4.1–5.0, on
PostgreSQL and MySQL.

**[Full list of changes in CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/grinchenkoedu/local_cleanup/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#30---2026-08-30)** — there are five breaking changes; the ones that need
you to do something are below.

## Upgrading from 2.x

Copy the new files over `local/cleanup` and run the Moodle upgrade as usual. Then check four
things — the upgrade handles the rest.

**1. Managers can now open the reports.** 2.x let only site administrators in. 3.0 grants
`local/cleanup:view` to the `manager` archetype, so managers can see both reports, including
file owners' names. If that is not what you want, revoke it at *Site administration → Users →
Permissions → Define roles → Manager*.

**2. Nobody but a site administrator can delete.** `local/cleanup:deletefiles` is granted to no
archetype at all, because it destroys content irreversibly. Administrators keep it. If someone
else needs it, grant it deliberately.

**3. Unlinked files will not be removed for the first week.** A file now has to be seen
unlinked by two scans at least `ghostgracedays` apart — 7 by default — before it is removed.
Existing rows are not backfilled, so the first scan after the upgrade counts as the first
sighting and the list will sit still for a week. This is working as intended: content uploaded
between two scans can deduplicate onto a hash an earlier scan recorded as unlinked, and 2.x
destroyed those files.

**4. Delete any `$CFG->cleanup_*` lines from `config.php`.** Your settings are migrated
automatically into the plugin's own namespace and the old database values removed, but the
upgrade cannot edit `config.php`. Anything left there is dead and will mislead the next person
who reads it. The settings now live at *Site administration → Plugins → Local plugins →
Clean-up*.

Your existing configuration carries over, including the components you were cleaning: a site
that had auto-remove on keeps backups and assignment submissions ticked, matching the pair 2.x
hardcoded. A site that had it off starts with nothing ticked and deletes no component files
until you choose one.

## Worth doing once

See what it would remove before letting it act:

```sh
php local/cleanup/cli/cleanup.php
```

That is new in 3.0, it reports and touches nothing, and `--execute` is what makes it act. On a
large backlog, set `maxrecordsperrun` first so the first real run does not overrun your cron
window.
